Definition: properly, to flow as water (i.e. to rain); transitively, to lay or throw (especially an arrow, i.e. to shoot); figuratively, to point out (as if by aiming the finger), to teach
BiblicalUsage: Yârâh is the word for teaching, for pointing the way as an archer aims at the mark. Samuel promised to teach Israel the good and the right way, and Solomon prayed that God would teach His people the good way wherein they should walk. The Levites were to teach Jacob God's judgments and Israel His law, so that teaching and the law belong together.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe teaching is aiming, and the teacher's work is to point the learner at the mark and not let him wander. My position is that God Himself is the teacher of His people, and every human teacher only repeats His lesson. And I hold that the good way is not a guess but a road God has already marked, and He will teach me to walk in it.
